tasks.short: Help staff resolve computer problems and escalate cases needing specialist diagnosis.

steps.what: Record requests received through the {EMAIL}, {CHAT}, or phone in the {HELPDESK}.
Find relevant guidance and previous resolutions in the {HELPDESK} and {DOCS}.
Discuss symptoms and guide the employee through suitable checks.
Apply a standard remedy using administration tools and confirm it helped.
Prepare an incident packet for unresolved cases in the {HELPDESK}.

loop.input: Ticket conversation, recorded checks, and remedy results.
loop.output: Structured incident packet with symptoms, attempted remedies, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link statements to ticket entries; analyst checks omissions and sensitive content.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; incomplete packets return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates populate fixed fields, but variable conversation text needs summarising.

steps.what: Send the outcome and update ticket status in the {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: Configure channel intake, approved-guidance search, standard remedies, and outcome notifications in the {HELPDESK}. A bounded drafting loop prepares unresolved incident packets, while analysts retain difficult conversations and approve remedies that change an employee's environment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance was inconsistent, channel intake required retyping, and standard remedies lacked reliable eligibility checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured service workflows already handle much of the structured work. A small text loop can prepare escalation summaries without automating the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Vague symptoms, accessibility needs, and frustrated employees require patient interaction. Identity checks and permission boundaries must remain reliable.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst recognises confusion, adapts explanations, and helps employees recover confidence as well as functionality.

ambition.what: Mobile self-service guidance for field staff without regular access to a staffed desk.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer ticket-entry and status-update chores and more difficult support conversations. Routine remedy authority remains within existing permissions; broader decision rights do not follow automatically.

reach.task: Improve support access for staff working away from desks.
reach.learn: Workplace service design, accessible instructions, and channel adoption.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk supports ticket summaries and drafts knowledge items for review.
Microsoft reports fewer internal IT tickets after introducing self-service assistance; its scale and missing baseline limit transferability.
Configured intake, guidance search, remedies, and notifications are established service-management patterns.
The time shares and pilot build ranges are estimates, not documented customer results.

assumptions: A {HELPDESK} exists and contains reusable guidance.
Administration tools occupy {OTHER}; the pilot covers approved standard remedies only.
Conversation remains the largest step, consistent with the communication prior.
Outcome notices go to the requesting employee within the organisation.
GDPR applies to support records; national consultation rules apply if the change introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: Supported intake channels and existing channel connectors.
Quality, ownership, languages, and accessibility of approved guidance.
Which remedies are already authorised for service desk staff.
Whether field staff can authenticate from mobile devices.
Required access approvals and national consultation procedures.
research_questions: Can existing configuration provide useful guidance search without generated answers?
Which standard remedies expose eligibility checks, execution logs, and safe failure responses?
new_work: Review escalation summaries and correct missing context.
Maintain guidance, remedy eligibility rules, and channel mappings.
Handle failed self-service attempts and inaccessible instructions.
tasks.statement: Provide staff and users with assistance solving computer-related problems, such as malfunctions and program problems.

tasks.short: Monitor systems, test changes, coordinate maintenance, and verify installations.

steps.what: Inspect health, capacity, and update status in monitoring and administration tools.
Agree maintenance scope and acceptable disruption with the service owner.
Write test cases and installation checks in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Changed specification, existing tests, and maintenance plan.
loop.output: Draft additional tests and installation checks.
loop.check: Analyst checks coverage; tests run in isolation and include known failing examples.
loop.stop: One draft and two repair attempts; unresolved failures return to manual test authoring.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing tests are reused directly; changed behaviour needs new scenario interpretation.

steps.what: Run regression, performance, and installation tests using test automation tools.
Coordinate the agreed installation window and send internal notices through the {EMAIL}.
Approve readiness and install the release through deployment and administration tools.
Check post-installation health and update maintenance records in the {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: Configure health checks and maintenance findings in the {HELPDESK}, with test and deployment jobs orchestrated through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded loop drafts additional tests; the {PROJECT} holds readiness evidence and approval before deployment, while the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL} handle agreed windows and notices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests, schedules, deployment steps, and monitoring were managed separately. Environment differences and incomplete rollback procedures made unattended execution unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration and deterministic jobs can connect existing monitoring, tests, and deployment tools. Coding assistance helps create missing tests and connectors without replacing release approval.
tasks.still_hard: Representative test data, hidden dependencies, realistic performance tests, and rollback after data changes remain costly. Employee-related monitoring requires GDPR controls and assessment under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges whether test evidence reflects real business use and negotiates disruption across dependent teams.

ambition.what: Weekly maintenance prioritisation using measured failure risk and business impact.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking screens and arranging routine installations toward test coverage and dependency risk. The analyst can recommend smaller maintenance batches more often; production approval remains with the service owner.

reach.task: Coordinate dependencies across a maintenance release.
reach.learn: Release planning, critical paths, readiness criteria, and stakeholder commitments.

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents can generate test plans and tests and attempt repairs; generated tests still need coverage review.
Aikido Security provides code, dependency, and cloud scanning that can support release checks.
The Netherlands has works-council consent rules relevant to employee-monitoring systems; national requirements elsewhere vary.
Deterministic orchestration, time savings, and build ranges here are design estimates for one service.

assumptions: The pilot covers one service with a usable test environment and deployment interface.
Monitoring, test automation, and deployment tools occupy {OTHER}; each category is named in its step.
Health checks and test execution are more structured than the overall judgement prior; release risk remains human.
Scheduling automation uses agreed windows and routes conflicts back to the analyst.
Post-installation failures create exceptions rather than successful maintenance records.
Consultation effort is included; applicable national procedures may increase elapsed time.
unknowns: Current test coverage, deployment tooling, and environment similarity.
Whether deployment and rollback can run without interactive access.
Service dependencies, maintenance commitments, and approval thresholds.
Whether proposed metrics identify or evaluate individual employees.
Applicable national consultation rules and access lead times.
research_questions: Which existing tools already support scheduling, health checks, and gated deployment?
Can rollback and post-installation checks be demonstrated in a representative environment?
new_work: Review generated test coverage and maintain realistic test data.
Investigate failed checks, scheduling conflicts, and deployment exceptions.
Maintain thresholds, dependency maps, credentials, and rollback procedures.
tasks.statement: Test, maintain, and monitor computer programs and systems, including coordinating the installation of computer programs and systems.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain application code that meets agreed business needs.

steps.what: Clarify requested behaviour, constraints and acceptance examples with the process owner.
Inspect source repository, development tooling and relevant interface documentation.
Choose component boundaries, data handling and failure behaviour.
Write application code and tests in development tooling.

loop.input: One scoped change design, acceptance examples, permitted source files and interface definitions.
loop.output: A draft code change and tests in an isolated branch.
loop.check: Compile, run existing regression tests, check independent acceptance examples and scan dependencies and code.
loop.stop: At most three draft-and-check attempts per change; unresolved failures return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle scaffolding, but bespoke behaviour requires interpreting requirements and existing code.

steps.what: Run automated build, regression and security checks in development tooling.
Review behaviour and maintainability, then approve merging in source repository tooling.
Approve deployment and release through deployment tooling.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} to hold scoped acceptance criteria and configure source repository and development tooling in {OTHER} to supply bounded change context. Generate standard scaffolding deterministically, then use a bounded model loop for bespoke code drafts. Configured checks produce evidence, while separate review and release approvals control merging and deployment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Custom behaviour required substantial hand coding, while weak acceptance examples made generated changes difficult to verify.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can draft scoped changes, and established build and scanning tools provide repeatable checks. Benefits depend on repository quality and reviewer effort.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous requirements, architectural consequences, missing regression coverage and failures that appear only under real workloads.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether behaviour solves the business problem and whether the code will remain understandable.

ambition.what: Small operations-tool change service

tasks.altitude: The analyst can spend more of the week testing business behaviour and delivering small improvements. They can recommend which small changes to attempt; merge and production decision rights remain explicit and separate.

reach.task: Slice requested improvements into independently releasable changes.
reach.learn: Dependency management, acceptance criteria and release sequencing.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance and review features with expected human oversight.
Aikido Security provides code, dependency and cloud scanning and proposed fixes.
Field experiments reported more completed developer tasks, but do not establish this team's expected gain.
A randomised study found experienced developers took longer with AI, supporting local measurement.

assumptions: The analyst writes modest application changes; larger engineering work is shared with developers.
Existing source repository, build and deployment tooling are represented by {OTHER}.
Build estimates cover the assistance workflow for one repository, not rebuilding an application.
The model loop has no production credentials and cannot merge or deploy.
A named reviewer can assess generated code independently of its generated tests.
Access includes checking source-code and personal-data handling under GDPR. Employee consultation under national rules applies if the workflow introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: What regression coverage and acceptance examples already exist?
Which code and data may be supplied to model processing?
Who has merge and deployment authority?
Does existing tooling support isolated branches and reproducible checks?
Would usage measurement require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which recurring changes can be replaced entirely by templates or existing configuration?
Does assistance reduce elapsed delivery time after review and rework are included?
Which independent tests detect plausible but incorrect implementations?
new_work: Review generated drafts and reject unnecessary complexity.
Maintain acceptance examples and test fixtures.
Handle failed model attempts and newly discovered vulnerabilities.
Measure delivery time, rework and defects without unnecessary employee monitoring.
tasks.statement: Use object-oriented programming languages, as well as client and server applications development processes and multimedia and Internet technology.

tasks.short: Discuss clients' information needs and agree what a system must do.

steps.what: Read the client request and supporting documents in the {EMAIL} and {DOCS}.

loop.input: Client request and authorised supporting documents.
loop.output: Discussion brief with stated needs, source references and open questions.
loop.check: Analyst checks claims and removes inferred needs presented as facts.
loop.stop: One brief and one correction pass; missing context becomes an explicit question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests describe needs inconsistently and often mix symptoms with proposed solutions.

steps.what: Arrange a discussion through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Explore needs, examples and tradeoffs with the client representative.
Write requirements and unresolved questions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Analyst discussion notes, client examples and requirements template.
loop.output: Requirements draft distinguishing agreed needs, assumptions and open questions.
loop.check: Analyst verifies traceability to notes and checks for invented agreement or commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous requirements remain open.
loop.why_not_simpler: Conversation notes need semantic interpretation before they become clear requirements.

steps.what: Confirm requirements and correct misunderstandings through the {EMAIL}.
Record confirmed requirements and follow-up actions in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} coordinates invitations and copies confirmed requirements into the {PROJECT}. Small bounded loops prepare a discussion brief and requirements draft from authorised material in the {EMAIL} and {DOCS}; the analyst conducts the conversation and the client confirms the requirements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs emerge through dialogue, while notes, confirmations and project records are maintained separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and approval features handle coordination. Bounded drafting can turn analyst notes into a consistent review document.
tasks.still_hard: Clients may disagree internally, omit constraints or describe a preferred solution before explaining the underlying problem.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst notices hesitation, challenges assumptions and builds enough trust to uncover the real need.

ambition.what: A pre-project requirements clinic for small departmental requests.

tasks.altitude: Conversations remain central, with less preparation and follow-up administration. The analyst gains time to challenge weak requests, but gains no new authority to commit budget or delivery dates.

reach.task: Turn confirmed requirements into delivery scope and acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Scope control, dependencies and the distinction between a need and a delivery commitment.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, confirmation tracking and copying structured requirements can use configured workflows.
TOPdesk offers summaries and reviewed knowledge drafts, demonstrating bounded text assistance rather than requirements negotiation.

assumptions: Clients may be internal departments or external customers.
Discussion notes are written by the analyst; recording and transcription are outside the initial build.
Scheduling uses an authorised participant list, approved invitation text and shared availability links.
Step shares describe total workflow effort, including client confirmation.
unknowns: Whether clients can access the proposed confirmation channel.
Who has authority to confirm requirements.
Which confidentiality terms govern client material.
Whether the {PROJECT} supports the required configured integration.
research_questions: Do clients find the draft easier to correct than current meeting notes?
How often does drafting introduce an implied commitment absent from the notes?
new_work: Review briefs and requirements for unsupported conclusions.
Resolve overdue confirmations and disputed requirements.
Maintain templates, participant permissions and integration mappings.
tasks.statement: Confer with clients regarding the nature of the information processing or computation needs a computer program is to address.

tasks.short: Connect business systems so teams can share reliable information.

steps.what: Agree which information teams need to share and who owns it.
Inspect interfaces, field definitions, permissions and sample records.
Resolve field meanings, ownership, validation rules and acceptable sharing.
Configure connections and transformations between the source and destination.
Test transfers and reconcile counts, values, failures and duplicate handling.
Approve activation, confirm rollback arrangements and release the connection.

tasks.design: Configure supported connectors in the {WORKFLOW} between the {ERP} and {CRM}, using an approved integration contract. A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks schema changes, reconciles transfers and opens exceptions in the {HELPDESK}. The system owner approves production activation after reviewing test and rollback evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teams disagreed about field meanings, access was fragmented, and connector testing required repeated manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors handle standard transfers. AI coding can help build missing reconciliation checks, although local effort still needs measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting ownership, unsupported interfaces, historical data defects and changes to business meanings.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate what a shared record means and which team must resolve a disagreement.

ambition.what: Weekly integration health review

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time configuring transfers and checking totals, and more time resolving ownership and recurring defects. They can recommend corrective work weekly; authority to change business meanings remains with data owners.

reach.task: Define acceptance limits for shared operational records.
reach.learn: Sampling, defect severity and evidence needed to release a process change.

evidence.claim: Configured connectors and deterministic reconciliation can handle stable, explicitly mapped transfers.
AI coding assistance is available for building missing integration checks; this does not establish a deployment speedup.
GDPR applies to personal-data transfers; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed use.

assumptions: The example connects the {ERP} and {CRM}; the same pattern can serve other authorised system pairs.
Supported connectors and separate test environments exist. Bespoke application development is covered by the programming task.
The integration contract can express mappings, validation, retries and duplicate handling without model interpretation.
Estimates cover one modest integration and include access and applicable consultation effort. External waiting periods can extend elapsed time.
Production activation is gated; configuration and test writes occur in an isolated environment.
unknowns: Which systems, connectors, interface limits and licences are available?
Who can approve data sharing and production activation?
Does the transfer contain employee or other personal data?
Do national rules require employee consultation for this change?
research_questions: Can existing connector configuration express the mapping without custom code?
Which failures require reconciliation rather than simple retries?
What baseline measures capture transfer accuracy and time spent resolving exceptions?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and unexpected schema changes.
Maintain mappings, credentials and connector versions.
Retest duplicate handling and rollback after material changes.
tasks.statement: Coordinate and link the computer systems within an organization to increase compatibility so that information can be shared.

tasks.short: Agree system principles with management and record the resulting decisions.

steps.what: Gather existing principles, design decisions and unresolved exceptions.
Prepare a brief explaining choices, consequences and questions for management.

loop.input: A fixed evidence pack, existing principles and a short briefing template.
loop.output: A draft brief with cited choices, consequences, disagreements and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require source references for factual claims; analyst checks omissions, tone and unsupported implications.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per meeting; missing evidence becomes a question for management.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but summarising conflicting free-text arguments requires interpretation.

steps.what: Discuss priorities, challenge assumptions and negotiate acceptable system principles.
Approve principles, exceptions and named decision owners.
Publish decisions, notify affected teams and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Generate an evidence pack from approved records in the {DOCS} and unresolved work in the {PROJECT}, then use a bounded drafting loop for a reviewed discussion brief. Management negotiates and approves principles through a structured decision record. A configured flow in the {WORKFLOW} publishes approved decisions, sends internal notices through the {EMAIL} and assigns agreed actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work was reaching agreement, while preparation and follow-up were scattered across documents and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured decision records and configured flows can remove repeated copying. Bounded drafting can shorten briefing preparation without replacing negotiation.
tasks.still_hard: Competing incentives, budget tradeoffs, trust and management's willingness to make an explicit decision.
tasks.human_edge: Build agreement across interests and recognise when apparent consensus hides unresolved objections.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling briefs and distributing decisions, with more room to prepare difficult conversations. Decision rights do not change; management remains accountable for principles and exceptions.

reach.task: Translate approved principles into project constraints and escalation points.
reach.learn: Governance, stakeholder mapping and decision escalation.

reach.task: Coordinate operational adoption of an agreed system principle.
reach.learn: Service ownership, practical rollout constraints and communication needs.

evidence.claim: Structured decision records can drive deterministic publication, internal notifications and action assignment.
TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for review, demonstrating reviewed drafting of internal explanatory text.
Negotiating system principles requires accountable human choices; document automation does not establish agreement.

assumptions: Management already meets to resolve system principles and exceptions.
Approved decisions can be captured in structured fields before publication.
Notifications use the approved decision text and agreed recipients.
Estimates cover one decision template, one approval route and existing internal systems.

Access review covers GDPR and confidentiality. Employee consultation under national rules is included where a proposed principle affects employees; wider implementation consultation is outside this small briefing workflow.
unknowns: Who has authority to approve principles and exceptions?
Where are authoritative decisions currently stored?
Which decisions can be distributed broadly?
Do proposed principles affect employee monitoring, work organisation or other consultation rights?
research_questions: What information does management repeatedly lack when a decision is deferred?
Can existing approval and notification configuration cover the entire publication step?
Does a shorter reviewed brief improve decision clarity without omitting dissent?
new_work: Review briefing drafts for missing objections and unsupported implications.
Maintain decision templates, approval routes and distribution groups.
Resolve overdue actions and outdated principles.
tasks.statement: Consult with management to ensure agreement on system principles.

tasks.short: Modify an existing system to support a new purpose or improve a workflow.

steps.what: Observe the workflow and clarify the requested improvement with users.
Inspect configuration and dependencies, then choose the smallest viable change.
Implement configuration or code changes in a development environment {OTHER}.

loop.input: Approved change design, selected source files, configuration schema and acceptance criteria.
loop.output: A proposed change package and tests in an isolated development environment.
loop.check: Validate configuration schema, run tests and security checks, and review the diff against acceptance criteria.
loop.stop: At most two generation attempts per change package; unresolved failures return to the developer. No production credentials.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native configuration first. Bespoke transformations require translating requirements into code that fixed templates cannot fully express.

steps.what: Run regression and integration checks in a test runner {OTHER}.
Try representative work and confirm operational acceptance.
Deploy the approved change through deployment tooling {OTHER}.
Update operating instructions and close the change record.

tasks.design: Use native configuration in the {WORKFLOW} first, then add narrowly scoped code only where needed. A bounded drafting loop prepares custom changes in a development environment {OTHER}; deterministic checks produce evidence in {PROJECT}, and deployment tooling {OTHER} releases only accepted, approved changes. Templates update change records in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small improvements still required scarce development time, integration knowledge and manual release coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted drafting can shorten some coding work, while existing test runners and deployment controls handle repeatable execution. Local measurement must establish the actual gain.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented dependencies, weak test coverage and conflicting user needs remain expensive. Passing tests does not establish that a workflow is useful.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst decides whether the proposed change solves the real process problem and recognises consequences outside the written request.

ambition.what: A fortnightly small-workflow improvement clinic for departmental process owners.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing improvement hypotheses with users and less time assembling change paperwork. They can select reversible pilot designs within an agreed scope; release rights remain explicitly assigned.

reach.task: Sequence a small change around dependencies and release constraints.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, rollout planning and outcome-based acceptance.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supports code completion, review and coding-agent workflows with human oversight.
Field trials involving 4,867 developers reported 26% more completed tasks; this does not establish the same gain for systems-analysis work.
METR found experienced developers slower in its early-2025 study; its later rerun was inconclusive.

assumptions: The first build covers one reversible workflow change with a test environment.
Most implemented behaviour is deterministic; model use is confined to development drafts.
Representative test data and rollback mechanisms are available.
GDPR and the EU AI Act are assessed against the changed workflow, including any employee-related decisions.
unknowns: Which changes can existing configuration support?
How much regression coverage already exists?
Who approves acceptance and production deployment?
Does the change require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which repeated change types can become configuration templates?
Does assisted drafting reduce time to an accepted release after review and rework?
new_work: Review generated changes and maintain acceptance tests.
Triage failed checks and unexpected integration behaviour.
Maintain deployment templates and verify rollback procedures.
Measure operational outcomes after release.
tasks.statement: Expand or modify system to serve new purposes or improve work flow.

tasks.short: Interview workers and observe tasks to understand how information is processed.

steps.what: Prepare interview questions and a sampling plan in the {DOCS}.
Arrange worker interviews and observation sessions through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Interview workers about inputs, decisions, workarounds and information passed to others.
Shadow workers or perform representative tasks and note actual information flows.
Consolidate findings into a process map and exception register in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Authorised interview and observation notes with session references.
loop.output: Structured process steps, information handoffs, exceptions and conflicting accounts.
loop.check: Validate the schema; analyst checks source references and preserves contradictory accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per session bundle; unsupported steps remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Workers describe the same activities differently and observations contain contextual free text.

steps.what: Validate the process map and exceptions with workers and the business process owner.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} schedules sessions and supplies standard observation forms from the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop converts analyst notes into structured findings, and deterministic rendering produces a process map for validation with workers and the process owner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Much of the useful evidence was situational, and consolidating notes required careful interpretation. Recording activity would not reveal why workers made particular choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms and scheduling reduce coordination work. Bounded extraction can organise notes while retaining source references and disagreements.
tasks.still_hard: Workers may change behaviour when observed, and rare exceptions may be missed. GDPR and national employee consultation rules govern relevant personal-data collection; extending the tool to staff assessment requires a fresh EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst earns trust, sees tacit workarounds and distinguishes a flawed process from an individual's adaptation.

ambition.what: Include occasional and part-time process users in discovery sessions.

tasks.altitude: The analyst keeps interviews and observation, but spends less time scheduling and consolidating notes. Within the agreed study scope, they can choose additional cases to investigate; they gain no authority to rate workers.

reach.task: Investigate where a documented procedure differs from actual work.
reach.learn: Sampling, evidence traceability and separating process defects from individual performance.

evidence.claim: Structured forms, reusable guides and deterministic rendering can reduce discovery administration.
SharePoint autofill demonstrates prompt-based document metadata extraction and warns that outputs can be wrong.
In the Netherlands, arrangements for observing staff behaviour or performance can require works council consent.
EU AI Act Annex III includes certain employment and worker-management uses, making intended purpose relevant.

assumptions: The typical case uses interviews and observation; broad surveys are optional.
The initial build uses analyst notes without audio capture or individual activity tracking.
Standard guides provide a starting point; the analyst chooses questions and sampling.
Effort estimates cover one process study with existing {DOCS} and {CALENDAR} access.
unknowns: Which national employee consultation requirements apply.
Whether workers can participate during paid working time.
Whether notes identify individuals or contain sensitive personal data.
Which shifts, locations and occasional users are currently missed.
Whether hands-on task trials require training or operational permission.
research_questions: Does the generated map preserve disagreements and rare exceptions accurately?
Does broader sampling reveal materially different information flows?
How much consolidation time remains after checking generated findings?
new_work: Review extracted findings against notes.
Maintain interview guides and source-reference conventions.
Remove unnecessary identifiers and apply retention rules.
Arrange follow-up observation for disputed or missing process paths.
tasks.statement: Interview or survey workers, observe job performance, or perform the job to determine what information is processed and how it is processed.

tasks.short: Determine the software, hardware and capacity needed for a proposed system change.

steps.what: Clarify workloads, user needs and service constraints with the business lead.
Inspect asset records and infrastructure management consoles for capacity and compatibility.
Read technical manuals and support terms to identify configuration constraints.

loop.input: Versioned manuals, support terms and the system inventory.
loop.output: Draft constraints with source passages, versions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each constraint; analyst verifies critical compatibility and support limits.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting material goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Compatibility conditions appear in varied prose and tables. Fixed rules handle known fields only.

steps.what: Calculate sizing, licence quantities and indicative costs in a comparison workbook.
Choose a configuration and document assumptions, alternatives and unresolved risks.
Approve the resource specification or return it for revision.

tasks.design: A read-only integration brings asset and capacity records from the {HELPDESK} and infrastructure management tools in {OTHER} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop prepares cited constraints from the {DOCS}; deterministic calculations generate sizing scenarios and a draft resource specification. The analyst chooses the configuration, and the IT manager approves its use in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory, support conditions and sizing assumptions sit in separate places. Maintaining their mappings often costs more than preparing an occasional specification.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, calculators and templates. Bounded document extraction can assist with prose; neither removes the need to verify assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete inventories, uncertain demand, licence interpretation and unusual dependencies. Access and employee consultation can take longer where infrastructure data exposes staff activity.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which service risks and capacity margins are acceptable when demand and business priorities conflict.

ambition.what: Quarterly capacity headroom decisions for order processing.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing demand scenarios and resolving service trade-offs. Approval and spending rights do not change.

reach.task: Translate seasonal order volumes into system capacity scenarios.
reach.learn: Peak arrival patterns, operational bottlenecks and the cost of delayed processing.

reach.task: Turn the resource specification into a phased implementation estimate.
reach.learn: Delivery dependencies, lead times and contingency planning.

evidence.claim: Inventory integration, sizing calculators and specification templates are feasible with conventional software.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrate prompted document extraction; Microsoft warns that extracted values can be wrong.
Developer field trials found productivity gains, but do not establish a 10-to-100-fold speedup for this solution.

assumptions: Ranges estimate a pilot for one system family with usable exports or read APIs.
The system inventory contains configuration and aggregate capacity data, rather than individual productivity measures.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the actual data and use. Consultation follows national rules.
The time split retains substantial human discussion and configuration judgement, consistent with the task priors.
unknowns: Inventory completeness and available read access.
Whether existing configured reports already cover the required inventory and sizing.
Approved demand forecasts, service targets and licence interpretations.
Whether national consultation requirements apply to the proposed data collection.
Who may approve resource specifications and capacity trials.
research_questions: Which sizing rules can be tested against previous changes and observed capacity?
How often do extracted compatibility conditions omit an important version limitation?
Does an existing inventory report make a new connector unnecessary?
new_work: Verify critical extracted constraints and resolve conflicting manuals.
Maintain inventory mappings, sizing formulas and price dates.
Investigate stale or missing capacity data.
Compare predicted capacity with observed results after implementation.
tasks.statement: Determine computer software or hardware needed to set up or alter systems.

tasks.short: Train staff to use systems through relevant practice, guidance and follow-up.

steps.what: Discuss learner roles, difficult tasks and accessibility needs.
Prepare instructions, demonstrations and practice exercises.

loop.input: Approved operating instructions, learner roles, learning needs and synthetic practice examples.
loop.output: Role-specific instructions and exercises with source references.
loop.check: The analyst performs each exercise, checks instructions against the current interface and verifies accessibility.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per module; unsupported instructions are removed or written by the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but adapting explanations and exercises to different roles requires language generation.

steps.what: Arrange sessions, enrol learners and send joining instructions.
Demonstrate tasks, coach practice and respond to learner questions.
Check exercise results and identify who needs further practice.
Record attendance and arrange agreed follow-up support.

tasks.design: Configure enrolments, scheduling, objective exercise checks and reminders through the {LMS} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded drafting loop turns approved material in {DOCS} into reviewed training packs, while the analyst leads practice and interprets learning difficulties. Repeated questions become reviewed guidance in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training material went stale, and coordination consumed time around each session. Useful teaching still depended on knowing the learners and their work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning and scheduling features can remove administration. Bounded drafting can prepare role-specific material from approved instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Learners differ in confidence, language, accessibility needs and prior experience. A completed exercise may conceal poor understanding.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer notices confusion, creates psychological safety and adjusts the explanation while someone attempts real work.

ambition.what: Short practice sessions for shift staff who cannot attend standard daytime training.

tasks.altitude: The week contains more coaching and less scheduling or document assembly. The analyst can adjust lesson order and practice formats within agreed learning goals; no new employment decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Arrange staff coverage so learners can attend practice sessions.
reach.learn: Shift constraints, service coverage and accessible scheduling.

TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for review, supporting the narrower pattern of reviewed guidance preparation.
Using AI to evaluate workers can bring the use within the EU AI Act employment category; training administration alone does not establish that classification.

Live practice remains the largest time component, consistent with the task's communication-heavy prior.
Learning checks support coaching and do not automatically rank staff or determine employment outcomes.
GDPR applies to learner records. Employee consultation and record access depend on national rules.
unknowns: Which enrolment and scheduling features are already available?
Which learner groups need language or accessibility adaptations?
Who may see individual learning results, and how long are they retained?
Is consultation required for changes to learning records or assessment?

Can learners complete representative tasks independently after the session?

Maintain source instructions and remove outdated guidance.
Review ambiguous exercise results and arrange additional coaching.
Maintain enrolment rules, access permissions and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Train staff and users to work with computer systems and programs.

tasks.short: Translate processing needs into feasible system designs and agreed specifications.

steps.what: Interview process owners about needs, constraints and troublesome cases.
Inspect configurations, interfaces and representative processing records.
Document processes, data entities, relationships and unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Requirements notes, permitted current-state evidence and a fixed modelling schema.
loop.output: Draft requirements, process relationships and data entities with source references and open questions.
loop.check: Validate schema and references; compare technical entities with observed definitions; analyst checks business meanings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per evidence pack; unresolved claims remain explicit open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Schemas generate technical diagrams directly, but interview notes express implicit requirements in free text.

steps.what: Compare design options against capacity, cost, security and operational constraints.
Validate the proposed design and agree requirements and tradeoffs.
Publish the agreed specification and link requirements to delivery work.

tasks.design: Collect permitted configuration evidence from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} through scheduled read-only jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Generate technical diagrams from schemas and use a bounded extraction loop to turn notes in the {DOCS} into traceable draft requirements. After owners agree the design, deterministic templates publish the baseline in the {DOCS} and linked work in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was dispersed, diagrams drifted from actual systems, and interview notes needed careful manual interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Schema extraction and document generation are established techniques. Bounded text extraction can reduce transcription work while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Unspoken needs, conflicting priorities, uncertain future loads and operational consequences that only users can explain.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the real problem behind a requested feature and make defensible tradeoffs under uncertainty.

ambition.what: Design clinics for small operations teams

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time copying evidence and maintaining specifications, leaving room for smaller teams' design questions. They gain capacity to recommend experiments; budget and design approval rights remain with the relevant owners.

reach.task: Assess whether process changes could remove the need for a system feature.
reach.learn: Process observation, benefit measurement and organisational change.

reach.task: Define recovery requirements for a proposed system design.
reach.learn: Business impact analysis, dependencies and recovery tradeoffs.

evidence.claim: Schema extraction and templates can generate technical documentation and traceability records.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrates prompt-based document metadata extraction; its documentation warns of incorrect results.
Extracting useful requirements does not establish that a proposed architecture meets business needs.

assumptions: The example concerns an operational process using the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Process owners provide notes and representative cases; meeting recording is unnecessary.
Estimates cover one process area, a fixed modelling schema and a small set of evidence sources.
Evidence collection uses minimum necessary data under GDPR, without introducing individual employee performance analysis.
Access and consultation estimates include applicable national rules; formal consultation can add elapsed waiting time.
unknowns: Which system metadata can be exported reliably?
Are process maps and capacity baselines current?
Who can approve requirements, architecture and operational risk?
Does the evidence contain personal data or commercially sensitive material?
Which national consultation requirements apply to proposed process changes?
research_questions: Which models can be generated directly from technical definitions?
How often do extracted requirements omit exceptions or confuse preferences with obligations?
Can users validate a small prototype before committing to a full design?
new_work: Review source references and resolve extracted ambiguities.
Maintain modelling schemas and evidence connectors.
Refresh baselines when interfaces or approved requirements change.
Check whether small-team design clinics produce useful, actionable decisions.
tasks.statement: Analyze information processing or computation needs and plan and design computer systems, using techniques such as structured analysis, data modeling, and information engineering.

tasks.short: Evaluate packaged applications and adapt the selected option to local workflows.

steps.what: Agree essential workflows, constraints and evaluation criteria with users.
Collect application documentation, supplier answers, prices and contractual limitations.

loop.input: A fixed set of supplied documents and responses mapped to evaluation criteria.
loop.output: An evidence register containing quoted support, source locations and unanswered criteria.
loop.check: Require a source location for every extracted claim; the analyst checks mandatory criteria and flags contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting material goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier evidence uses varied prose and layouts. Structured questionnaires are imported directly when available.

steps.what: Compare application fit, total cost, integration risk and exit options.
Configure shortlisted applications in sandbox environments {OTHER} with representative workflows.
Perform representative work in application sandboxes {OTHER} and discuss usability.
Approve application selection, accepted gaps and adaptation scope.
Apply approved settings to the selected application {OTHER} and record the handover.

tasks.design: A structured evaluation register in the {WORKFLOW} combines deterministic cost calculations with bounded extraction from supplier material in {DOCS}. Native application configuration and reusable test cases support pilots in sandbox environments {OTHER}; users supply usability evidence before selection. Approved settings are applied through supported application controls {OTHER}, with handover records stored in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier claims, costs and pilot findings were difficult to compare consistently. Each evaluation repeated document reading and sandbox setup.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence registers, reusable configuration templates and bounded extraction reduce preparation work. Existing application controls handle adaptation where they expose suitable configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier claims can omit limitations, and short pilots miss operational friction. Integration depth, licensing terms and exit costs need direct verification.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges which compromises users can live with and tests claims against actual work.

ambition.what: A low-cost application fit check for small departmental purchasing requests.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time copying claims and more time testing the most consequential gaps. They can design pilots within an approved budget; purchasing and release authority require an explicit mandate.

reach.task: Assess the service and staffing consequences of an application purchase.
reach.learn: Whole-life cost, support arrangements and how process changes affect office operations.

evidence.claim: Evidence registers, cost calculations and sandbox configuration can support application evaluation without automating selection.
SharePoint autofill demonstrates extraction of document content into metadata, with possible errors requiring review.
The digest provides no documented case proving end-to-end application selection or adaptation savings for this task.

Native configuration is sufficient for the pilot; substantial custom development is scoped separately.
Supplier purchasing commitments remain outside automated actions.
GDPR and EU AI Act checks follow the intended application use. Employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Consent and access ranges are working-effort estimates; formal consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which applications allow sandbox access and configuration export?
Are comparable prices, contract terms and exit provisions available?
Who can approve selection, spending and production settings?
Does the proposed application monitor or evaluate employees?
research_questions: Which mandatory requirements need a live demonstration rather than documentary evidence?
Which pilot settings can be transferred through supported configuration controls?
Which recurring evaluation criteria predict problems after adoption?
new_work: Check extracted claims and pursue missing supplier evidence.
Maintain evaluation criteria, cost formulas and configuration templates.
Refresh pilot scenarios as local workflows change.
Verify configuration drift and support ownership after adoption.
tasks.statement: Assess the usefulness of pre-developed application packages and adapt them to a user environment.

tasks.short: Agree system goals and draw the logical flows needed to achieve them.

steps.what: Review the change brief, existing diagrams and system constraints in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Change brief, process map and system documentation.
loop.output: Constraint notes with source references and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Analyst checks critical constraints against cited passages; unsupported claims are rejected.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per brief; unreadable or conflicting sources return to analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Constraints appear in varied prose and diagrams without consistent fields.

steps.what: Discuss outcomes, scope and conflicting priorities with the business process owner.
Write measurable goals and logical operating rules in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Goal decisions, constraint notes and specification template.
loop.output: Goal specification and structured logical specification with explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and branch references; analyst checks goals, exceptions and assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved business choices remain marked for discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning negotiated outcomes into operating rules requires interpreting free text.

steps.what: Draw program flows and decision branches from the logical specification.
Review goals and flows, resolve exceptions and approve the design baseline.

tasks.design: A generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} turns a reviewed logical specification into diagrams and checks missing branches and unreachable steps. Bounded reading and drafting loops prepare specifications from the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} records approval of the design baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagrams were maintained separately from requirements, and narrative constraints needed manual interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured specifications, diagram generation and bounded text extraction can be assembled with less custom development. Coding assistance can reduce build effort, but a universal speed multiplier is unsupported.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing what success means and finding undocumented exceptions remain costly. A valid diagram can still describe the wrong process.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst exposes conflicting goals and tests whether the proposed logic fits actual work.

ambition.what: A design impact preview showing which process branches change under a proposed requirement.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time drawing and more time testing alternatives with process owners. Within agreed project scope, they can choose which design alternatives to investigate; business priorities still require owner approval.

reach.task: Assess the operating impact of a proposed process change.
reach.learn: Process measures, exception costs and how to compare the current and proposed flow.

evidence.claim: Structured specifications can drive deterministic diagram generation and consistency checks.
GitHub Copilot supports coding assistance with human oversight; this does not establish the proposed solution's time savings.
Developer productivity evidence varies; METR's early study found slower work and its later rerun was inconclusive.

assumptions: The first build covers one process family and an existing {DOCS}.
Step shares are illustrative task effort, not measured customer time.
The logical specification can use a common schema for branches, inputs and outputs.
unknowns: Whether existing diagrams match current operations.
Which diagram formats teams must edit or export.
Who can approve scope and business rules.
Whether source documents contain personal or restricted information.
research_questions: Can the proposed schema represent real exception paths without hidden narrative rules?
Does generating diagrams from specifications reduce total revision effort in a pilot?
new_work: Check extracted constraints and unsupported assumptions.
Maintain the logical specification schema and diagram templates.
Resolve validation failures and keep source references current.
tasks.statement: Define the goals of the system and devise flow charts and diagrams describing logical operational steps of programs.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain system design procedures, test procedures and quality standards.

steps.what: Read existing procedures, design records, defects and audit findings.
Agree acceptance criteria, risk tolerances and required evidence with delivery and quality leads.
Draft or revise design procedures, test instructions and quality standards.

loop.input: Approved quality criteria, existing sections and relevant design evidence.
loop.output: A sectioned procedure draft with traceable changes and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections and references; analyst checks changed instructions against design evidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; unresolved policy or design questions remain explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but adapting instructions to changed designs requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Write test cases and scripts in test-management and source-repository tools.

loop.input: Acceptance criteria, interface definitions, test templates and approved sample data.
loop.output: Draft test cases and scripts linked to acceptance criteria.
loop.check: Check syntax, scan code and run in isolation; analyst checks assertions and missing failure cases.
loop.stop: One generation and two repair attempts per routine; remaining failures return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable tests use templates. New application behaviours require contextual translation into checks and assertions.

steps.what: Run test routines in a test runner and retain results.
Review coverage and approve the procedure pack or request changes.
Publish the approved revision and update procedure links.

tasks.design: Configure linked evidence views in the {PROJECT} and versioned templates in the {DOCS}. Bounded loops draft changed procedure sections and new test routines; a configured test runner in {OTHER} executes checks in isolation and retains results. Approval by the quality lead triggers publication and link updates through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures, design evidence and tests drift apart. Templates reduce formatting work but cannot decide which controls a changed system needs.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes generators and traceability checks cheaper to build. Bounded drafting can handle changed prose and test code while existing runners perform deterministic validation.
tasks.still_hard: Good assertions, representative test data and coverage of failure modes. Passing generated tests can hide a shared misunderstanding of the requirement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful quality thresholds and challenge whether the evidence would reveal a serious failure.

ambition.what: Release-readiness packs for small operations teams without dedicated quality staff.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time designing failure scenarios and coaching delivery teams. Authority to approve standards remains with the quality lead.

reach.task: Translate operational failure modes into acceptance criteria and evidence requirements.
reach.learn: Risk-based sampling, control effectiveness and defect escape analysis.

reach.task: Add recovery and degraded-service checks to release readiness.
reach.learn: Recovery dependencies, exercise design and evidence of successful restoration.

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents generate test plans and tests and repair failures; this supports test drafting capability, not reliable coverage.
GitHub Copilot offers coding and review assistance with human oversight.
The cited Veracode tests found substantial security problems in generated code, supporting independent checks of test helpers and scripts.
Versioned templates, approval-triggered publication and deterministic traceability checks are conventional implementations.

Established test runners and document approval features are configured before adding custom code.
The quality lead has authority to approve the procedure pack.

Whether requirements have usable acceptance criteria.
Test-data sensitivity and permission to create representative samples.

What proportion of maintenance effort comes from changing interfaces rather than drafting?

Maintain templates, traceability rules and isolated test environments.
Investigate flaky tests and unexplained coverage gaps.
Check that publication uses the exact approved revision.
Retire obsolete procedures and test routines.
tasks.statement: Develop, document, and revise system design procedures, test procedures, and quality standards.

tasks.short: Use logs and performance data to diagnose code faults, test fixes and release corrections.

steps.what: Inspect logs and performance indicators in the {OTHER} monitoring system.
Compare diagnostic evidence with recent changes and known incidents in the {HELPDESK}.
Reproduce the failure and decide its cause in the {OTHER} development environment.
Correct code and add a regression test in the {OTHER} code repository.

loop.input: Reproduced failure, approved cause assessment and a scoped source-code snapshot.
loop.output: Candidate patch and regression test in an isolated branch.
loop.check: Analyst reviews the diff; the regression test must fail before the patch and pass afterward.
loop.stop: At most two patch attempts within the specified files; failed checks return to analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Novel faults require changes to code logic that fixed templates cannot express.

steps.what: Run tests and inspect results in the {OTHER} build pipeline.
Review test evidence, operational impact and rollback before approving release.
Deploy the approved correction through the {OTHER} deployment pipeline and verify recovery.

tasks.design: Configured monitoring in the {OTHER} monitoring system feeds diagnostic evidence to the {HELPDESK}; deterministic joins on the {DATA_PLATFORM} connect failures with releases and known signatures. A bounded loop drafts a patch in the {OTHER} code repository, while the {OTHER} build and deployment pipelines enforce tests, release approval, health checks and rollback rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs, release history and incident records were disconnected. Novel faults still required bespoke diagnosis and code changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing monitoring and pipelines can handle collection, checks and deployment. Coding assistance can draft a scoped correction once a person establishes the cause.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent failures, weak tests and incomplete telemetry limit automation. GDPR requires proportionate handling of personal data in logs; staff monitoring can also trigger consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes correlation from cause and weighs the operational risk of a correction.

ambition.what: A weekly recurring-fault prevention review using linked incident and release evidence.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling evidence and executing repeatable checks, and more time reproducing difficult failures. They can prioritise technical investigation within the incident process; release authority remains with the change approver.

reach.task: Validate recovery assumptions for a critical application.
reach.learn: Recovery objectives, rollback limits and the evidence needed to demonstrate restored service.

Field trials involving 4,867 developers found more completed tasks; this does not establish autonomous fault resolution.
Security logging should be necessary and proportionate.
In the Netherlands, staff-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent under article 27.

Digital logs and test output replace the historical task's reference to printouts.

Repair flaky tests and rehearse rollback procedures.
Review access, consultation requirements and telemetry scope when monitoring changes.

tasks.short: Compare equipment or software options and recommend a justified choice.

steps.what: Agree evaluation criteria, budget assumptions and adoption constraints with the business sponsor.
Read supplier proposals, specifications and commercial terms against the criteria.

loop.input: Received proposals, specifications, commercial terms and evaluation criteria.
loop.output: A cited fact table separating quoted facts, supplier claims and missing answers.
loop.check: Validate currencies, dates and units; analyst checks material price, support, security and exit conditions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; ambiguity remains flagged for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposal formats and contractual wording vary. Fixed parsers handle standard fields but miss qualified claims.

steps.what: Calculate comparable costs and score evidenced features in an evaluation workbook.
Discuss trial results, practical fit and adoption trade-offs with service owners.
Choose a preferred option and explain trade-offs, risks and implementation conditions.
Endorse the preferred option or request further evidence.

tasks.design: Use the {PROCUREMENT} and {DOCS} as the proposal record, with a bounded extraction loop preparing cited comparison facts. Deterministic calculations produce cost scenarios, an options matrix and a recommendation template from agreed criteria. The analyst judges fit with service owners, and sponsor endorsement in the {PROJECT} hands the recommendation to procurement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Infrequent evaluations use inconsistent proposals and one-off comparison workbooks. Normalising facts helps, but cannot settle conflicting priorities or adoption risks.

tasks.still_hard: Testing supplier claims, estimating migration and exit costs, and judging operational fit. Supplier clarification and contract review can dominate elapsed time.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge attractive claims, weigh organisational readiness and explain a recommendation that stakeholders can defend.

ambition.what: Software exit-readiness assessments for departmental system owners.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time on trials, migration risks and stakeholder decisions. Recommendation, purchasing and contract-signing rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess how a proposed system changes administrative workloads and service access.
reach.learn: Frontline work patterns, accessibility needs and adoption costs.

reach.task: Compare the expected operational benefit with migration and exit costs.
reach.learn: Benefits measurement, sensitivity analysis and process-change evaluation.

tasks.short: Read technical material and test examples to learn how to meet user requirements.

steps.what: Turn a user requirement or knowledge gap into specific technical questions.
Find relevant manuals, technical reports and articles in documentation portals and document stores.
Read selected sources and identify relevant techniques, limitations and examples.

loop.input: Retrieved passages from the approved source set and specific technical questions.
loop.output: A short findings draft with exact citations, version limits and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check that citations resolve and passages support each claim; analyst reads decisive passages in context.
loop.stop: One answer and one correction pass per question; unsupported questions return source links without an answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search retrieves passages, but relating varied technical explanations to a particular requirement needs language interpretation.

steps.what: Try documented examples in a development sandbox and assess their fit.
Record useful findings, source versions and cautions for later design work.

tasks.design: Configure version-aware search over an approved source catalogue in the {DOCS}, including links to technical documentation portals in {OTHER}. A bounded reading loop returns cited findings, and a deterministic template assembles source versions and sandbox results into reusable notes. The analyst checks decisive passages, tries examples and approves shared findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Search returns documents rather than a checked answer to a specific implementation question. Source versions and local requirements are difficult to keep aligned.

tasks.still_hard: Learning enough to notice a misleading answer still takes practice. Restricted manuals, conflicting versions and undocumented behaviour limit coverage.
tasks.human_edge: Build an accurate mental model, recognise missing context and test whether a technique actually fits the requirement.

ambition.what: Version-change impact briefs for project managers.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time locating passages and more time experimenting and explaining consequences. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess how a platform version change affects the delivery plan.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, schedule uncertainty and how to express technical findings as delivery consequences.

reach.task: Check whether documented recovery methods work in a representative sandbox.
reach.learn: Recovery objectives, restoration evidence and operational dependencies.

METR's early developer study found slower work with AI; its later update describes uncertainty, supporting local measurement.
The later METR update does not establish a settled productivity estimate for current tools.

tasks.short: Lead systems projects, coordinate technical work, and supervise programmers or analysts.

steps.what: Review milestones, assignments, dependencies, and overdue work.
Collect missing updates and consolidate reported blockers.

loop.input: Updates submitted for the current project reporting period.
loop.output: Blockers, dependencies, reported owners, and missing information with source references.
loop.check: Validate project identifiers and dates; the project lead checks ambiguous ownership and unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per update; unresolved items return to the project lead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Current updates contain free text whose wording varies. Structured forms can replace extraction where adopted.

steps.what: Assess technical dependencies, delivery risks, and sequencing options.
Agree priorities and approve changes beyond delegated scope or capacity.
Coach team members, resolve disagreements, and agree practical next actions.
Update assignments, dates, dependencies, and decisions in project records.
Prepare and circulate the project progress report.

tasks.design: Configure a delivery dashboard and structured decision and action records in the {PROJECT}, with approved changes updating assignments automatically. A bounded loop extracts blockers from submitted updates in the {EMAIL} and {CHAT}; a deterministic template produces a progress report in the {DOCS} for review. Technical tradeoffs, sponsor decisions, and coaching remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates arrive in different formats, and decisions made in meetings require repeated entry. Existing reporting also depends on consistent project records.

reach.learn: Dependency modelling, capacity planning, and forecast calibration.

reach.task: Investigate recurring handoff delays between operational teams.
reach.learn: Process observation, root-cause analysis, and outcome measurement.

Check that reporting supports coordination without becoming employee scoring.
tasks.statement: Supervise computer programmers or other systems analysts or serve as project leaders for particular systems projects.

tasks.short: Design and implement integrated systems that solve production, inventory, and cost-analysis problems.

steps.what: Agree the business problem, decisions, and success measures with process owners.
Extract operational and cost data from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}.
Reconcile identifiers, units, and costing definitions using a {SPREADSHEET}.
Build the integration and analysis view using development tools and the {BI}.

loop.input: Approved mapping specification, interface schemas, requirements, and code templates.
loop.output: Draft transformations, interface code, analysis view, and tests.
loop.check: Static and security checks, sandbox execution, reconciliation totals, and analyst review.
loop.stop: One draft and two repair cycles per component; unresolved failures return to manual implementation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Configure existing capabilities first; remaining custom transformations require interpreting written requirements.

steps.what: Reconcile outputs and demonstrate representative scenarios to process owners.

tasks.short: Prepare cost-benefit and return-on-investment analyses for proposed systems investments.

steps.what: Confirm the problem, alternatives, analysis horizon, and intended business outcomes.
Export current operating costs, transaction volumes, and project effort.
Collect proposals and identify implementation, subscription, migration, and support costs.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and internal estimates for the agreed alternatives.
loop.output: Source-linked cost items with currency, charging period, exclusions, and uncertain terms.
loop.check: Validate numeric fields and units; the analyst checks material costs and all ambiguous terms against sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; missing or conflicting terms remain flagged for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals describe charging terms and exclusions in varying prose and layouts. Standard cost forms should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Set benefit assumptions, adoption scenarios, risks, and treatment of released staff time.
Calculate cash flows, return, payback, and sensitivity across alternatives.
Write the business case, recommendation, uncertainties, and comparison of alternatives.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, source references, assumptions, and the analyst's chosen recommendation.
loop.output: Business-case narrative linked to calculated results and stated uncertainties.
loop.check: Insert financial tables deterministically; verify narrative numbers against results and require analyst review of causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported claims are removed and unresolved sections return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Project-specific explanations connect qualitative risks and benefits. Fixed templates can handle routine cases without a loop.

steps.what: Challenge assumptions with finance and approve, defer, or reject the investment.

tasks.design: A versioned calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines approved exports from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, and {PROJECT} with an assumption register, then generates a financial model and scenario tables. Bounded loops extract source-linked proposal terms and draft the business case in the {DOCS}; the analyst reviews both. Finance challenges the assumptions, and the investment sponsor approves the investment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each analysis combines different proposals, cost definitions, and benefit assumptions. Reusable calculations were possible, but source mapping and document preparation remained bespoke.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation code, validation rules, and document templates can be built with coding assistance. Small extraction and drafting loops handle variable prose without controlling the financial calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Attributing benefits, estimating adoption, and distinguishing released capacity from cash savings remain judgement calls. Missing baseline data can dominate uncertainty even when arithmetic is correct.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic benefits, expose who must change behaviour, and explain when a strategically useful investment has weak measurable returns.
